findings.claim: Every container that leaves the port by road travels I-16 westbound toward distribution centers in Macon, Atlanta
findings.correctedValue: False as stated. GPA: about 80% of Savannah's cargo moves inland by truck and 20% by rail (a record 545,214 rail containers in 2025; 42 double-stack trains a week from the Mason Mega Rail Terminal to Atlanta, Memphis, Nashville, Charlotte, Orlando). Road access: Garden City Terminal trucks use the Jimmy DeLoach Parkway (a $129M limited-access truck route linking the terminal with I-16 (exit 152) and I-95; about 5,000 trucks a day to I-95), SR 307/Dean Forest Road to I-16 exit 160, the Brampton Road Connector (opened July 15, 2026) toward I-516, and Ocean Terminal's $29M overpass to U.S. 17/I-16. Suggested: 'About 80% of the port's containers leave by truck, and many of those reach I-16 at Dean Forest Road, the Jimmy DeLoach Parkway or I-516 before heading west toward Macon and Atlanta; others take the Jimmy DeLoach Parkway to I-95.'

findings.claim: FMCSA violations: Federal regulation violations constitute negligence per se in Georgia courts
findings.correctedValue: Overstated. Accurate: 'Georgia has adopted the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations as state rules, including for intrastate trucking (O.C.G.A. § 40-1-8; Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 515-16-4-.01; Ga. DPS Transportation Rulebook ch. 1), so a violation can support a negligence per se claim under O.C.G.A. § 51-1-6 — but the injured person must still show the violation caused the crash (Parris v. Gooch, Ga. Ct. App. June 24, 2026; Parker v. R & L Carriers, Ga. Ct. App. 2002).' Note O.C.G.A. § 40-1-8(h) itself requires motor carriers to comply with 49 C.F.R. Parts 391, 392 and 395.
findings.quote: At the time of the collision, Georgia had adopted the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations ('FMCSR') as its own safety regulations applicable to intrastate commerce. ... The complaint asserted claims for negligence and negligence per se against Parris, with the negligence per se claims premised in part on alleged violations of the FMCSR.
findings.sourceName: Parris v. Gooch, Nos. A26A0423-0425 (Ga. Ct. App. June 24, 2026), citing Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 515-16-4-.01 (2021)
